page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7T83 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs executing across 1 physical core with 2 threads, clocked at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of memory-heavy virtualization profiles. The instance operates without integrated local disk storage and features no dedicated GPUs, relying on remote block storage and virtual network connectivity with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth under the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-thread performance paired with constrained aggregate throughput due to the dual-thread core configuration. The instance registers an above-average stress-ng single-core score of 2691.19 and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1494.0. In contrast, multi-core metrics sit in the lower quartile, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core rating of 1854.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3141.52. Memory bandwidth tests yield 26.05 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 12.61 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks reflect these operational limits, showing 2.05 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 2.18 GB/sec in static web serving.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7a.large serves as an accessible entry point for workloads needing a generous RAM footprint without incurring the expense of higher core counts. The primary tradeoff lies in compute concurrency, as heavy parallel compilation, dense database operations, or intensive ray tracing saturate the single physical execution core quickly. The instance is functionally aligned with lightweight caching layers, small in-memory key-value stores, staging databases, and background enterprise services requiring low vCPU intensity alongside substantial operating memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at 2.55 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server pairs 16.0 GB of system memory with 32 MB of L3 cache, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying on standard network-attached storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results demonstrate capable single-core throughput alongside modest multi-core capacity, consistent with its dual-thread hardware allocation. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 26.05 GB/sec, while write speeds measure 12.61 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost-effective RAM density for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than compute parallelization, making it suitable for lightweight Redis deployments, intermediate caching, and modest memory-bound background tasks.
